management_steps.details: Onset: sudden/thunderclap (SAH), post-traumatic. Symptoms: altered GCS, seizure, focal neurology, meningism (meningitis), fever. Comorbidities: malignancy, pregnancy (pre-eclampsia), HIV. Medications: anticoagulants.

Tension: bilateral pressure/tightness, mild-mod. Migraine: gradual unilateral pulsating, photophobia, visual auras, mod-severe. Cluster: rapid peri-orbital excruciating, ipsilateral eye redness/lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, Horner's syndrome, severe.
Tension: NSAIDs, Paracetamol. Migraine: Metoclopramide, triptans, NSAIDs, consider steroids. AVOID OPIOIDS! Cluster: 100% Oxygen high flow, paracetamol, triptans, steroids, ketamine if refractory.
